notes:
**One address in your footer is no longer reported as thirty-one.**

A site that prints the same address on every page — which is nearly every
site — was told it had dozens of "address variations" and advised to
standardise a format that was already identical everywhere.

Docket reads the whole page including the footer, and by that point the
navigation has been flattened into one run of words with no punctuation
between it and the address below. The address pattern anchors on the postcode
and reads backwards, so it swept up whatever the breadcrumb happened to say —
"Home Learning UNISON Centre, 130 Euston Road, London NW1 2AY" on one page,
"Our podcasts UNISON Centre, …" on the next. A different breadcrumb on every
page meant a different "variation" on every page.

Measured on a trade union's site, 2026-09-02: one address, published
identically on all 217 pages crawled, reported as 31 variations. It now reads
as one.

Addresses are compared from where the street line starts — the house number,
or a unit word like "Suite" — so genuine mismatches ("Rd" against "Road",
"Ste 210" against "Suite 210") are still reported, and the finding now lists
the spellings it counted so you can check the number yourself.
